title: 06 Vectors: Visual Guide
outline: 1. Modulus Becomes Magnitude | the same arrow read as a complex number a + bi and as a vector <a, b>, with an operation toggle comparing add, scale and multiply-by-i | modulus is magnitude and argument is direction, so vector notation is the complex plane minus the multiplication rule

2. Length And Heading | a magnitude slider and a direction slider building the components <r cos t, r sin t>, then recomputing magnitude and direction back out of them | components and magnitude-with-direction are the same information, 0 degrees gives <6, 0> and 90 degrees gives <0, 6>, and inverse tangent needs a quadrant fix

3. Stretch Flip Collapse | a multiplier k dragged from -3 to 3 against a vector, with the line through the origin drawn and the two half-scaled mistakes marked | a scalar lengthens, shortens, reverses or collapses but never rotates, both components scale, and |k v| = |k| |v|

4. Tip To Tail | u and v with an add/subtract toggle, the second arrow redrawn from the first arrow's tip, and the length comparison beside the components | adding is componentwise and drawn tip-to-tail, subtracting is adding the opposite, and magnitudes do not add

5. Boat And Current | three word-problem scenarios - boat plus current, walk east then west, two forces - with the second vector on sliders and the resultant read back in compass words | name the axes first, translate every phrase into components, add, and convert back to magnitude or direction only at the end
